verdict_reason: The declared estimand -- mean per-token [cos(h, W_target) - cos(h, W_deranged)] on the centred output projection -- is computed correctly, and the two identities the file claims for it hold: the margin is the mean of per-token differences (not a difference of means) and the derangement is a genuine fixed-point-free permutation of the SAME label multiset. I CONFIRM codex's heterogeneous-row defect at consistency.py:158,248,275 and quantify its reach, which codex did not: `_safe_unit(x.float())` narrows AFTER centre_and_rescale has already factored out a power of two, so a row whose magnitude is below ~1e-45 of the matrix maximum underflows to zero and contributes cosine 0. I swept it -- with the large rows fixed at 1e25 the small rows give the exact margin 2.0 at q = 1e25, 1, 1e-5, 1e-10, 1e-13, 1e-16 and 1e-20, and 0.0 only at q = 1e-30 -- so the failure needs a within-matrix row-magnitude ratio of ~1e-45, which no unembedding matrix has. Normalising in double and narrowing afterwards returns 2.0 at every rung.
comparable_reason: The statistic is a cosine in the residual-stream basis, and that basis is not canonical: the reparameterisation h -> hA, W -> W A^{-T} leaves the model's function EXACTLY unchanged and changes the metric completely. Measured on a 64x16 fixture with A = diag(a, 1, ..., 1): max |logit change| 1.776e-15 at every a, while the headline moves -0.057886725268 -> -0.051732527348 -> -0.015284397267 -> +0.000580325018 -> +0.000094930873 for a = 1/2/10/100/1000 -- a sign flip and a 100% change with the function held fixed. A bias-compensated shift of the hidden origin does the same: offset 0/1e2/1e4 gives -0.057886725268 / -0.000577366631 / -0.000005789800. Two models that implement the same function in different bases are therefore not comparable on this column, and no model's basis is privileged.
github_reason: No released implementation exists: this is a BLME-original diagnostic and task_metadata carries no upstream repository. The nearest published relative, the logit lens / tuned lens (AlignmentResearch/tuned-lens), computes logits through the unembedding, not a cosine margin against a frequency-matched control -- and the code's own measurement records that the two are not proxies for each other (Spearman(cosine over vocab, logit over vocab) = -0.2246 on gpt2, argmax agreement 3.4%). I verified the estimator by re-implementing the shipped path independently instead.
paper_reason: There is no source paper and no published scalar. The available anchors are analytic and BLME reproduces them: on an exactly antipodal two-label fixture where the true margin is 2.0 by construction, the task returns 2.0 across the whole scale range from 1e25 down to a row ratio of 1e-45; on the centred four-row simplex the declared value 4/3 is returned as 1.3333332538604736 (5.96e-08 relative, float32 rounding).
confounds_reason: Not a width proxy -- zero-padding is exactly neutral for a cosine -- but confounded with something worse: an arbitrary choice of coordinates. The GL(d) reparameterisation above changes the number by 100% and flips its sign with zero change to the model's function, so any cross-model ordering of this column partly encodes how each training run happened to scale its residual-stream coordinates. The frequency-matched control removes the anisotropy confound the file documents (raw cosine is reproduced to within 0.1-1.1% by a UNIFORMLY RANDOM vocabulary row across the whole cross-model range, which is why the raw key is correctly demoted to _meta_), but no control can remove a basis dependence.
defects: CODE / NARROWING BEFORE ROW NORMALISATION, THREE SITES (consistency.py:158 for the target and hidden rows, :248 for the frequency control, :275 for the uniform control). centre_and_rescale correctly promotes to float64 and factors out a power of two, and safe_unit_rows_torch is exact at any representable scale -- but `.float()` sits between them, so the helper never sees the data it was written to protect. Reproduced: margin 0.0 against the analytic 2.0 at a row ratio of 1e-45; exact 2.0 at 1e-40 and above; double-normalisation returns 2.0 at every rung. Identical defect class to matrix_entropy.py:116, and the fix is the same one-line move.

DOCUMENTATION / THE PUBLISHED DESCRIPTION IS OF A DIFFERENT NUMBER. docs/tasks_geometry.md section 12 and docs/interpreting_results.md:102 both describe `prediction_alignment_mean` as 'cosine similarity between each final hidden state and the lm_head.weight row for its target token'. That quantity is emitted, but under `_meta_prediction_alignment_raw_mean`, and the code demotes it precisely because it carries no target information. The headline is the centred, derangement-controlled MARGIN, which has a different sign, a different magnitude and a different interpretation. docs/tasks_geometry.md also says the task is 'Heavily dependent on generation parameters like temperature and top-p' -- the task performs no generation at all.
COMPARABILITY (not an implementation defect): 100% change and a sign flip under a function-preserving change of basis.

PROTOCOL: the frequency control orders equal-sized label groups by numeric token ID, so which position receives which control label is decided by an arbitrary vocabulary index. The permutation itself is correct (Sattolo, fixed-point-free, same label multiset), and the residual-collision rate is emitted -- but the CHOICE of control among the many valid derangements is not canonical.

GOOD PRACTICE WORTH KEEPING: when no document has more than one label the headline goes NaN and the raw cosine is emitted under its own name rather than silently standing in for the margin; the control collision rate is emitted as a corpus property; and the per-token margin is used so that the reported std matches the reported mean.
fix: Move the narrowing after the normalisation at all three sites: `_safe_unit(h.float())` -> `_safe_unit(h.double()).float()` (and likewise for target_embs at :158, the frequency control at :248 and the uniform control at :275). A unit-norm row is bounded by 1 in every coordinate, so narrowing after the division is unconditionally safe, and the analytic 2.0 anchor is then returned at every row ratio down to 1e-55. Separately, correct docs/tasks_geometry.md section 12 and docs/interpreting_results.md:102 to describe the emitted headline (the derangement-controlled margin on the CENTRED projection) rather than the demoted raw cosine, and delete the temperature/top-p sentence. For cross-model reporting, state explicitly that the number is basis-dependent, or replace the cosine with a reparameterisation-invariant quantity such as the target's rank or normalised logit under the model's own unembedding.
